title: Restriction of O-modules along an open immersion preserves colimits and quasi-coherence
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme] (for instance the inclusion of an open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$, or an isomorphism). For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal M|_X$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module with $(\mathcal M|_X)(U)=\mathcal M(f(U))$ for $U\subseteq X$ open, restriction maps those of $\mathcal M$, and $\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting through the isomorphism $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(f(U))\cong\mathcal O_X(U)$; a morphism $\alpha$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules goes to $\alpha|_X$ with $(\alpha|_X)_U=\alpha_{f(U)}$. Then: (1) $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathcal M|_X$ is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ which is left adjoint to the direct image $f_*$, hence preserves all small colimits: if $(\mathcal M,(c_i))$ is a colimit of a diagram $(\mathcal M_i)$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules then $(\mathcal M|_X,(c_i|_X))$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal M_i|_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; (2) if $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], so is $\mathcal M|_X$.
